plan.title: rfc(swarm,ux): Gap D parent-chat interactivity is not first-class on Grok Build — harness matrix + workaround evidence

narratives.Description: rfc(swarm,ux): Gap D parent-chat interactivity is not first-class on Grok Build — harness matrix + workaround evidence
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

**Operator experience (Grok Build):** asking for a swarm often turns the *same* top-level chat into a long-running orchestrator/monitor. The conversation pane stops accepting normal interaction until the operator interrupts. After interrupt, children may keep running; soft options (pause / save / resume after a network or machine change) are missing or destructive-only. The framework author treats this as a **miss relative to Gap D intent** and wants a first-class investigation — including whether Grok workarounds exist today, and whether newer Grok Build / model surfaces (e.g. evaluation on Grok 4.7 and successor harnesses) close the gap.

This issue is **not** "re-litigate Gap D prose." Gap D already shipped as doctrine. This issue is: **Gap D's operator-visible outcome is not first-class on Grok Build (and is uneven across harnesses)** — document combinations, enabling conditions, and a concrete exploration plan.

## Background (previous work)

### What Gap D is

From the 2026-06-22 Cursor incident, tracked and closed as doctrine in [#1880](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1880) (hotfix guidance slice; gate-code half routed to [#1877](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1877)):

- **Gap C** — worker lifecycle ownership (`drive-to: merge-ready` vs fragmented handbacks).
- **Gap D** — dispatch mode: long-running workers launched **foreground/blocking** locked the parent conversation; the rule is that workers expected to run >~3 min MUST be dispatched **independently / in the background** so the parent channel stays interactive and the orchestrator is notified on completion.

Canonical prose: `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` §9 (**Background / independent dispatch (Gap D)**), mirrored in swarm Phase 3 and review-cycle monitoring tiers. Incident rationale pointer: `docs/analysis/2026-07-02-agents-md-incident-rule-rationale.md` § Multi-agent orchestration discipline (#954) → Orchestrator dispatch doctrine (#1880).

**Important nuance:** closing #1880 shipped **guidance**, not a harness feature that forces parent interactivity. Gap D is a behavioral MUST for orchestrators when the host exposes a background primitive — not a guarantee that every host+Directive combo feels "chatty parent + mid-level swarm owner."

### Related host / topology work (do not conflate)

| Item | Role relative to this miss |
| --- | --- |
| [#1880](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1880) Gap D | Origin of the background-vs-foreground rule |
| [#3158](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3158) / [#3155](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3155) | Retain vs one-shot; nuclear-family A2A — orchestration messaging bounds |
| [#4130](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4130) | Grok nested `spawn_subagent` unsupported for leaf→monitor; parent owns sibling monitors |
| [#4286](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4286) | Grok parent-steer **file inbox** (not live chat / not `sessions_yield`) |
| [#4529](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4529) | Grok through-merge: implement `stop-at: pr-open` + named partner |
| [#2874](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2874) / [#2879](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2879) | OpenClaw parent announce / yield vs poll-wait patterns |
| [#2655](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2655) / review-cycle Approach 1–3 | Approach 3 blocking sleep poll **locks the pane** (must warn) |
| [#3984](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3984) (open) | Adjacent: parent-must-not-own multi-hour babysit did not bind — prose restatement alone insufficient; this issue focuses on **harness×Gap D fidelity** + Grok workaround evidence |
| `host-grok-build.md` | Documents no inventing `sessions_yield` / live `resume_from` on Grok |

## Goal

Make **parent steerability during long swarm / review ownership** an explicit, evaluable product surface:

1. **Clarify the contract** per harness: what "Gap D satisfied" means operationally (parent can accept a new user turn while cohort work continues; soft pause/steer paths named; interrupt semantics named).
2. **Map combinations** that allow vs prevent that outcome today (table below — refine with measured dogfood).
3. **Treat Grok Build as a first-class evaluation target**, not an afterthought: inventory real workarounds (two-session split, headless `swarm:launch`, steer inbox, completion-notify + yield discipline), measure whether agents follow them, and re-evaluate on **current and next Grok Build harnesses / models (including Grok 4.7 when available)** so we do not freeze conclusions on an old host snapshot.
4. **Decide disposition** after evidence: docs/operator card only, skill/host-adapter hardening, harness feature ask (xAI), Directive product verbs (pause/checkpoint cohort), or accept Grok as "spawn Tier-1 / parent-yield Tier-partial" with honest UX copy.

Success looks like: an operator reading one issue + one short doc knows *whether* their harness will keep the top chat usable during a swarm, *what* to do if not, and *what* we will re-test when Grok Build changes.

## Non-goals (for this issue's first pass)

- Replacing Gap D doctrine or reopening #1880 as failed delivery of prose.
- Implementing a full multi-orchestrator mesh / open A2A (forbidden by #3155).
- Promising soft "pause for home network" before we know host capabilities.
- Auto-ingesting unrelated RFCs (#4730 etc.).

## Harness combination matrix (starting point — validate)

Legend: **Full** = parent chat typically stays usable while long workers run, if agents follow Gap D. **Partial** = background spawn exists but parent often re-locks (monitor loops / no yield). **Weak** = operator must split sessions or accept lock/interrupt.

| Harness + Directive | Background primitive | Parent yield / soft steer | Typical operator outcome | What prevents Full |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OpenClaw** | `sessions_spawn` (+ visible) | `sessions_yield` / parent announce | **Full** (best documented match) | Agent ignores yield; nested spawn limits |
| **Cursor** | `Task` + `run_in_background: true` | Parent turn returns; completion notify | **Full → Partial** | Parent enters Approach 3 sleep poll; leaf ownership mistakes (#2797) |
| **Claude Code** | `Agent` + background | Parent turn returns if obeyed | **Full → Partial** | Same: parent re-locks; nest limits (#3134) |
| **Grok Build** | `spawn_subagent` (often background-capable) | No `sessions_yield`; no live `resume_from`; steer = `.deft-scratch/subagent-steer/` (#4286) | **Partial → Weak** (common: pane locks until interrupt; interrupt ≠ pause) | Parent stays in Phase 4–6 poll/`get_command_or_subagent_output`; Approach 3; nest ban pushes monitor into parent; missing soft pause/resume |
| **Grok Bot** | executor / CloudAgent (distinct from Build) | Host-specific; must not misclassify as `grok-build` (#4201) | **Unknown / measure** | Misclassification; background not used |
| **Warp / start_agent** | platform lifecycle | Historical cohort path | **Measure** | Ritual/provider assumptions from pre-Cursor world |
| **generic-terminal** | none | Approach 3 only | **Weak** (lock after warning) | No Tier-1 spawn |

### Conditions that *allow* Gap D's operator outcome

- Host exposes a **non-blocking** worker primitive AND a way for the parent turn to **end or yield** without waiting on the worker wall-clock.
- Completion reaches the parent via **notify/announce** (or equivalent), not only blocking `get_command_or_subagent_output` in the user-facing turn.
- Long review ownership is **Approach 1 sibling** (or leaf-owned blocking `pr:watch` *inside the leaf*), not Approach 3 in the parent pane.
- Operator (or skill) does not require the same session to be both all-day Phase 6 cascade and interactive research desk.

### Conditions that *prevent* it

- Foreground/blocking dispatch of implement/fix/monitor workers when background exists (classic Gap D recurrence).
- Parent tool-loop **busy-waits** on children (poll sleep, cascade inline) even after background spawn.
- Host lacks yield / message-later / soft pause (Grok today: documented in `host-grok-build.md`).
- Interrupt semantics = abort parent turn only; children orphan; no cohort checkpoint verb.
- Conflating "Tier-1 for spawn" with "Tier-1 for parent interactivity."

## Author stance (record explicitly)

The author considers the current Grok experience a **miss** against the spirit of Gap D: doctrine implies the top-level conversation remains usable; observed Grok Build behavior often does not. Prior belief that "Grok workarounds already make this fine" needs **evidence**, not assertion. This issue exists to explore those workarounds rigorously and to re-check when Grok Build / models move (including **Grok 4.7** and newer harness revisions), rather than declaring the platform permanently incompatible from one snapshot.

## Proposed exploration plan

1. **Dogfood matrix (measured):** for each row in the table, one short cohort or solo `drive-to` / babysit: can the operator send a new parent prompt within ~1–2 minutes of launch without interrupt? Capture harness version / model id.
2. **Grok workaround bake-off:** (a) two-session split (swarm owner vs research chat); (b) `task swarm:launch` prep + thin monitor session; (c) background workers + forced parent stop after spawn (no Approach 3); (d) steer-inbox soft redirect; (e) interrupt + REDISPATCH_OK recovery. Score each: chat usable? children controllable? resume after "go home"?
3. **Harness delta track:** re-run the Grok column when Build tools, `spawn_subagent` semantics, or models change (explicitly include Grok 4.7 evaluation). Record whether yield/retain/pause appeared.
4. **Disposition RFC comment:** docs-only operator card vs skill MUST hardening vs upstream harness ask vs new Directive pause/checkpoint surface — pick one primary, list leftovers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Issue body (or linked current-shape / design comment) keeps an accurate harness matrix with **allow/prevent conditions**, backlinking [#1880](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1880) Gap D and Grok-specific [#4130](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4130) / [#4286](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4286).
- [ ] At least one **measured** Grok Build dogfood note is posted (workaround bake-off scores), not only theory.
- [ ] Explicit re-evaluation checkpoint named for **newer Grok Build / Grok 4.7** (or "N/A — unavailable" with date).
- [ ] Written disposition: what we will tell operators *now*, and what product/docs change (if any) follows.
- [ ] No claim that Gap D prose was never shipped; the miss is **operator-visible fidelity on specific harnesses**.

## Type

enhancement / agent-experience / runtime-portability (swarm UX)

## References

- [#1880](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1880) — Gap C/D doctrine ship
- [#1877](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1877) — routing gate / Cursor wiring half

design-critique: warranted, because Gap D doctrine requires background dispatch so the parent channel stays interactive, and Grok Build commonly locks the top chat in a long orchestrator/monitor loop with no first-class yield, soft pause, or honest harness matrix.

## Gate stamp

P1 is operator-visible Gap D miss on Grok Build: parent pane stops accepting turns until interrupt; interrupt is not pause; children may orphan. Not a relitigation of #1880 prose. Open solution space: docs/operator card, skill hardening, upstream harness ask, Directive pause/checkpoint, or honest Partial/Weak copy. Round 1 open critique of #4796 at pin SHA `8b4be69db9dae571c72eb9dd8e2ebd49b601cf94`. Envelope ceiling `5736656147` (panel-deposit, inclusive). In-envelope comments: triage `5736647319`, deposit `5736656147`. Did not read later comments. Did not treat Gap D prose as failed delivery.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms)

Re-verified at the pin SHA. Line cites in the issue body are claims; these are the mechanisms they name.

| Mechanism | What it actually is | What it is not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gap D (`content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` §9; `core-phase-3.md`) | Orchestrator MUST background long workers so the parent channel stays interactive and is notified on completion. Cursor recipe is `run_in_background: true`. OpenClaw recipe is `sessions_spawn` + parent-announce. | A harness feature that forces parent interactivity. Closing #1880 shipped guidance. |
| `host-cursor.md` / `host-openclaw.md` | Each adapter carries an explicit Gap D spawn recipe plus a completion channel (Cursor notify / OpenClaw announce). OpenClaw completion is explicitly **not** `get_command_or_subagent_output`. | Grok's recipe. Phase 3 Gap D names Cursor, Claude `Agent`, and OpenClaw. It does not name `spawn_subagent`. |
| `host-grok-build.md` | First-class spawn via `spawn_subagent`. Monitor coordination is worktree git + `get_command_or_subagent_output`. Top-level MAY Approach-1 background a review-monitor. ⊗ invent `sessions_yield` or live `resume_from`. | A Gap D "background then end the parent turn" MUST. The adapter canonicalizes **pull-wait**. |
| #4130 nested-spawn boundary | Grok implementation leaf MUST NOT nested-spawn a review-monitor. Parent/orchestrator owns the sibling. Through-merge (#4529) forces implement `stop-at: pr-open` and Phase 6 / named partner as closer. | Permission for the parent pane to busy-wait. Nest-ban moves monitor ownership **to the parent**, it does not define how that parent stays interactive. |
| #4286 parent-steer inbox | Child-directed file inbox `.deft-scratch/subagent-steer/<agent-id>.json`, apply-once ack, `task verify:subagent-steer` exit 1 = `STEER_PENDING` (not `REDISPATCH_OK`). Writer is occupancy-owner or dispatching-parent. `text` is bounded and is not a new envelope. | Parent-chat yield. Heartbeat docs: "A scratch path does not interrupt a blocked tool." |
| #3158 one-shot default | `spawn_subagent` workers that finish the tool loop are observed terminal. Mid-scope gates are split-dispatch unless a live in_progress steer channel exists. | Soft pause / resume after interrupt. |
| #3153 durable owner | After `stop-at: pr-open` / human-merge, a reachable owner MUST remain for post-merge `scope:complete`. CLEAN is not lifecycle complete. | A license to end the parent turn with nobody on Phase 6. |
| Approach 3 (`deft-directive-review-cycle`) | Last-resort blocking sleep poll. MUST warn that it locks the pane. ⊗ when Approach 1/2 exists. | Grok's default. Grok is classified Tier-1 for **spawn**. |
| `evaluateParentTurnShape` | Library gate: tool-first, `yield` event, or one short answer after leaf announce (FC14). Legal yield is a generic event; skill prose names `sessions_yield` / OpenClaw. | A Grok host yield token. Nothing in this module invents one. |
| Heartbeat + `verify:subagent-alive` | Child→parent liveness on the Grok hybrid path because Phase 4 records **no native lifecycle channel** back to the monitor. | Completion notify. Complementary to, not a substitute for, a completion channel. |
| Headless `task swarm:launch` | C2 manifest PREP only. Does not spawn. Occupancy / dest-place (#4066) still bind the later spawn. | A second interactive parent. |
| #3984 (open, `design-critique:ingest-ready`) | Adjacent: parent-must-not-own multi-hour babysit did not bind, and another prose restatement will not. | This RFC. Different defect class (bind vs harness×adapter fidelity). Do not merge. |

## Injection / swarm lens

This target changes spawn envelopes, parent/child concurrency, one-shot `agent_id` identity (#3158), dest/occupancy shared state (#4066), worktrees, and the steer inbox (untrusted `text`).

- Steer `text` is already a closed, bounded, apply-once schema. Do not grow it into a new dispatch envelope or constitution edit (already ⊗ at pin SHA).
- A new pause/checkpoint verb is new shared state. The RFC non-goal ("do not promise soft pause before host capabilities") is the right fence. Interrupt + `REDISPATCH_OK` + `swarm:pre-dispatch` deny already cover orphan/replace. A pause that does not cancel occupancy races dest-lock.
- Two-session split is two parents, not an A2A mesh. Do not recut #3155. Do name who holds the swarm occupancy lease.
- Nest-ban (#4130) plus through-merge (#4529) means the **parent** is the only legal monitor owner. Any "parent stop" recipe must say how that owner re-enters.

## Findings

### 1. Bake-off (c) without a completion-notify conjunct drops the durable owner — `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** RFC exploration plan item (c) is "background workers + forced parent stop after spawn (no Approach 3)". Goal 3 lists "completion-notify + yield discipline" as a **separate** parenthetical, not as a conjunct on (c). At pin SHA, `host-grok-build.md` and Phase 4 say Grok monitor coordination is `get_command_or_subagent_output` and that the hybrid path has **no native lifecycle channel** back to the monitor. Envelope SLA #3153 requires a reachable owner after `stop-at: pr-open`. #4529 puts Phase 6 / named partner on that owner. #4130 forbids pushing the monitor into the implement leaf.

**Failure mode.** Harvest (c) as the Grok Gap D recipe. Parent ends the turn. No pull-wait, no documented completion re-entry. Phase 6 and leftover-complete have no owner. That is the RFC's own "interrupt ≠ pause; children may orphan" shape, now shipped as skill guidance. If a completion-notify **does** exist on a given harness snapshot, (c) is the correct Gap D shape (spawn, end turn, tool-first on announce) and is compatible with parent-owned sibling monitors. The plan as written does not make that measurement a gate on (c)'s legality.

**Disposition consequence.** The exploration plan cannot bind as written. Score (c) only when completion-notify (or a second session that **is** the durable owner) is measured true. Otherwise (c) is a #3153 defect, not a workaround. Do not bind an operator card that says "spawn and stop" without naming who owns Phase 6.

### 2. The Grok adapter never received the Gap D recipe the other Tier-1 adapters have — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Phase 3 Gap D at this SHA names Cursor `run_in_background`, Claude `Agent` background, and OpenClaw `sessions_spawn`. `host-cursor.md` MUST background long workers. `host-openclaw.md` MUST background and MUST use parent-announce, not `get_command_or_subagent_output`. `host-grok-build.md` has no equivalent Gap D MUST. It tells the parent to coordinate via `get_command_or_subagent_output`. Top-level MAY background a review-monitor is spawn permission, not parent-yield. The RFC matrix "What prevents Full" leads with no `sessions_yield` / no live `resume_from`, then lists parent Phase 4–6 poll.

**Failure mode.** Disposition picks "upstream harness ask" or "accept Partial/Weak" because yield is missing, while the cheaper recut is giving Grok the same adapter recipe Cursor/OpenClaw already have: background spawn, parent turn ends, completion arrives on a channel that does not require the user-facing turn to wait. Agents following `host-grok-build.md` **cause** the lock. That is not Gap D ignored; that is Gap D unimplemented on this adapter.

**Disposition consequence.** Bind the two-layer split as load-bearing, not as one Grok cell. Layer A: Directive adapter omitted the Gap D recipe and still mandates pull-wait. Layer B: host has no `sessions_yield` / retain. Skill/host-adapter hardening is not a leftover behind an xAI ask. The matrix column "Background primitive" is not the column "Parent yield". The RFC already says not to conflate Tier-1 spawn with Tier-1 parent interactivity; the Grok row still conflates them in one Partial→Weak verdict.

### 3. Steer-inbox bake-off (d) cannot score parent-pane usability — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** #4286 / `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md` / `packages/core/src/orchestration/subagent-steer.ts`: the inbox is parent→child, apply-once, `STEER_PENDING` is not takeover. "A scratch path does not interrupt a blocked tool." host-grok-build ⊗ invent `sessions_yield` on this path. RFC table already lists steer as the Grok yield substitute.

**Pane lock until interrupt.** Covered. Layer A recuts `host-grok-build.md` to the OpenClaw background-then-end-turn recipe and requires Phase 3 Gap D to name `spawn_subagent`. At this SHA the adapter still mandates pull-wait; agents following it cause the lock. Two trials attribute host vs adapter vs agent. Until a measured callback exists, Grok wording stays conditional.

**Interrupt is not pause.** Covered. The matrix split includes interrupt/orphan as its own axis. Bound-remedy refuses pause/checkpoint as primary. That is the honest-copy path from Stop 1's open solution space, not a pause verb.

**Children may orphan.** Covered. Scoring (c) without a durable owner is forbidden. Two-session occupancy prevents dest-lock steal. Trials record interrupt effect.
